title: Continuous conormal sequence for a formal power-series quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $D=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] with $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and put $R=D/I$ and $\mathfrak n_R=\mathfrak nR$. Set $\widehat\Omega_{D/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}$ and $\widehat\Omega_{R/F}=\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(R/\mathfrak n_R^r)/F}$ using [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with transition maps induced by quotient maps. For $B=D$ or $R$, let $\widehat{\mathrm d}_B:B\to\widehat\Omega_{B/F}$ be $b\mapsto(\mathrm d(b\bmod\mathfrak n_B^r))_r$, where $\mathfrak n_D=\mathfrak n$; write $\widehat{\mathrm d}$ with its domain understood. Then the sequence of $R$-modules $$R^{\oplus s}\longrightarrow\widehat\Omega_{D/F}\otimes_D R\longrightarrow\widehat\Omega_{R/F}\longrightarrow0$$ is exact (tensor base change [def-weil-module-base-change]), where the first map sends the $j$-th basis vector to the image of $\widehat{\mathrm d}(f_j)$ and the second sends $\widehat{\mathrm d}(h)\otimes\bar a$ to $\bar a\,\widehat{\mathrm d}(h\bmod I)$.

source.place: Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq, lines 34103-34155), quotient conormal sequence, and Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal, lines 34194-34209), comparison modulo powers. proof.text: Put $M=\widehat\Omega_{D/F}$, $T=M\otimes_D R$, $L=\sum_jR(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j)\otimes1)$, $N=T/L$, with quotient $q:T\to N$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n_R$. Apply [lem-trf-formal-conormal-quotient-data] with the stated $F,n,s,f_j$. For $r\geq1$ write $C_r=\Omega_{(R/\mathfrak m^r)/F}$, $p_r:M\to\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}$ for coordinate projection, and $u_r:\Omega_{(D/\mathfrak n^r)/F}\to C_r$ for the quotient-induced map. The lemma supplies $\iota:N\simeq\varprojlim_rN/\mathfrak m^rN$, the derivation $\delta(\bar h)=q(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(h)\otimes1)$, generators $\delta(\bar t_i)$ of $N$, and compatible maps $\phi_r:N\to C_r$ with $\phi_r(q(v\otimes\bar a))=\bar a\,u_r(p_r(v))$ and $\phi_r\delta(x)=\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$.

source.place: Assembly of returned conormal proof: Steps 1-4 extracted into the complete relation quotient lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-complete-derivation-truncation-reconstruction] with $k=F$, $d=n$, this $R,\mathfrak m,N,\delta,\iota,\phi_r$, and $x_i=\bar t_i$. The quotient $R=D/I$ is a commutative $F$-algebra; its ideal is $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n_R$. Completeness, generation, compatibility and differential formulas are exactly the conclusions of Step 1. Both inverse limits use the same positive indices $r\geq1$. It gives an isomorphism $\Phi:N\to C=\widehat\Omega_{R/F}$ whose $r$th coordinate is $\phi_r$. Its inverse is specified by the shifted formula $\Psi((c_r)_r)=\iota^{-1}((\eta_r(c_{r+1}))_r)$; both inverse identities are part of the cited statement.

source.place: Assembly of returned conormal proof: Steps 5-8 extracted into the shifted reconstruction lemma.

proof.text: The composite $b:T\xrightarrow q N\xrightarrow\Phi C$ is surjective and has kernel $L$, since $q$ is the quotient by $L$ and $\Phi$ is an isomorphism. The map $a:R^{\oplus s}\to T$ sending $e_j$ to $\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j)\otimes1$ has image $L$: its value at $(a_j)$ is $\sum_ja_j(\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(f_j)\otimes1)$. Thus $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$. For an arbitrary tensor $v\otimes\bar a$, Step 1 gives $(b(v\otimes\bar a))_r=\bar a\,u_r(p_r(v))$. In particular, for $v=\widehat{\mathrm d}_D(h)$ this coordinate is $\bar a\,\mathrm d(\bar h\bmod\mathfrak m^r)$, proving the asserted second-arrow formula by coordinatewise equality. For $n=0$, $D=F$ and $I=0$, so both continuous differential modules are zero; empty or redundant relation lists require no change to the quotient construction. No regular-sequence hypothesis or integer division is used.
